quiz.q: What does an IDE combine in one program?
options: Only a text editor with colours
Editor, compile and run, debugger and build tools
quiz.explain: An IDE integrates the tools you otherwise use separately; the Java version comes from the JDK you pick.

quiz.q: You open a new IntelliJ project without any JDK. What happens when you press Run?
options: IntelliJ compiles with its own compiler
It runs on the newest Java automatically
It stops: Project JDK is not defined
quiz.explain: The IDE calls the JDK's javac and java. No project SDK means nothing to compile with.

quiz.q: No red underline anywhere. What does this print?
quiz.explain: The string comes first, so + glues 3 and then 4 as text. The editor only catches errors, not logic.

options: Yes, printn is short for println
No: cannot find symbol, method printn
quiz.explain: There is no printn method. In an IDE, completion would have suggested println.

quiz.q: Where does IntelliJ show the output of your program?
options: In the Run window at the bottom
In the editor, next to the code
quiz.explain: The Run window shows the command it used, then your output, then the exit code.

quiz.q: What does this print when the project SDK is JDK 25?
quiz.explain: feature() gives only the main version number of the JDK that runs the code.

quiz.q: IO.println("Hi"); is red in IntelliJ, but you know it is valid Java 25. What do you check first?
options: The language level and project SDK
quiz.explain: With language level 23, IO and void main() are not normal Java yet, so the editor marks them red.

quiz.q: Which project SDK do you use for a Hyperskill project?
options: Any JDK, it does not matter
No JDK, the plugin has its own
quiz.explain: Hyperskill checks your code on JDK 23; Java 25-only code such as IO.println would not compile there.

quiz.q: Which statement about compact source files in IntelliJ is true?
options: They never work in an IDE
On JDK 25 they run like any program; on JDK 23 only with the preview language level
quiz.explain: Compact source files are final in Java 25 (JEP 512) and a preview feature in Java 23 (JEP 477).

flashcards.back: IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, VS Code with Java extensions.

flashcards.front: Does IntelliJ have its own Java compiler for your code?
flashcards.back: No. It uses the javac of the project SDK (a JDK).
The JDK one project compiles and runs with.

flashcards.front: What does the green Run button do?
flashcards.back: Compiles with javac and starts the program with java.

flashcards.front: Where do you find the full command IntelliJ used to run your program?
flashcards.back: On the first line of the Run window.

flashcards.front: What does a red underline in the editor mean?
flashcards.back: The code will not compile here.

flashcards.front: What does a yellow mark in the editor mean?
flashcards.back: A warning: it compiles, but something looks odd.

flashcards.front: Can code without any red underline still be wrong?
flashcards.back: Yes. Logic bugs compile and run.
A line where the debugger pauses the running program.

flashcards.front: Why is IO.println red with language level 23?
flashcards.back: IO is not part of normal Java 23; it was a preview feature then.
